issue.title: sase tool run orphans its child tree when the caller's process group is SIGKILLed (monitor 5s escalation, provider timeouts); run settles lost with no pgid
issue.description:
`sase tool run` puts its child in a new session (`spawn_child(..., start_new_session=True)` in
`src/sase/tool/executor_process.py`). Anything that kills the *caller's* process group with
SIGKILL therefore kills only the wrapper. The child tree (`just check` -> pytest ...) keeps
running as an orphan, and the ToolRun is later settled `lost`.

Two common callers do exactly that:

1. **Monitor/proc supervisors.** `sase.procs.supervisor._Termination` sends SIGTERM to the
   wrapper's pgid and escalates to SIGKILL after `_KILL_GRACE_SECONDS = 5.0`. The wrapper's own
   escalation (`TERM_ESCALATE_SECONDS = 5.0`, armed on the first 0.1 s wait tick) fires later,
   so the supervisor always wins the race whenever the child tree takes more than 5 s to exit
   on SIGTERM. Monitor timeouts and stops go through this path: 17 verify-monitor timeouts on
   athena in the week since 2026-09-15, and verify monitors now mostly run
   `-- sase tool run check`.
2. **Provider tool timeouts / agent kills** that SIGKILL the Bash tool's process group. There
   are 13 `lost` inline `check` runs in athena's ledger (of about 190 `check` runs).

The ledger can't say whether those trees were orphaned: `child_pid`/`child_pgid` are only sent
in `finish_tool_run`, so a `lost` run never records which group to check or reap.

Root cause: the child's process-group ownership doesn't follow the process owner, and the pgid
is recorded only at settlement. Likely fix directions (this needs a design decision):

- (a) when an enclosing monitor/proc owner is live, keep the child in the wrapper's process
  group and skip the wrapper's own escalation, so the owner's killpg reaches the whole tree;
- (b) record `child_pid`/`child_pgid` (plus the process identity) right after spawn, so
  `tool_run_reconcile` can reap a `lost` run's surviving group when the identity still matches;
- (c) optionally, for inline runs, make the child die with the wrapper.

Found while researching `sase tool` enforcement and monitor wrapping
(research:202609/sase_tool_guard_and_monitor_wrap__cld.md).

task_type_fields.impact:
Timed-out or stopped verify monitors, and agent Bash timeouts on inline `sase tool run check`,
can leave full `just check` / pytest trees running unowned. They burn CPU on an already
overloaded host (load 30+ is common), hold suite-gate worker tokens, and can write into
workspaces that have since been reused. The ToolRun reports `lost` with no pgid to reap. This
blocks making monitors wrap their commands in `sase tool run` by default, because every monitor
timeout would then go through this race.
task_type_fields.repro:
Run a supervisor-like parent with an isolated `SASE_HOME`. The TERM-ignoring child stands in
for a slow-to-exit `just check` tree:

```python
import os, signal, subprocess, time, tempfile
env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(("SASE_AGENT", "SASE_MONITOR", "SASE_PROC", "SASE_TOOL"))}
env["SASE_HOME"] = tempfile.mkdtemp()
p = subprocess.Popen(["sase", "tool", "run", "--", "sh", "-c", "trap '' TERM; sleep 37.4242"],
                     env=env, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)
time.sleep(3); os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
t = time.monotonic() + 5.0
while p.poll() is None and time.monotonic() < t: time.sleep(0.05)
if p.poll() is None: os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL)   # what sase.procs.supervisor does
p.wait(); time.sleep(0.5)
print(subprocess.run(["pgrep", "-f", "sleep 37.4242"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)
```

On athena (2026-09-22), 5 of 5 runs left `sh`+`sleep` alive and the ToolRun settled `lost`.
A plain `sase tool run -- sleep 23` whose caller group gets SIGKILL also leaves `sleep` running.

payload.entry: Fixed by epic sase-16h: sase-core 4b536cd (sase-16h.2) adds tool_run_observe and identity-matched reap candidates in reconcile; 5950d069c (sase-16h.3) spawns the child into the wrapper's process group under a live monitor/proc owner with no wrapper SIGKILL escalation, gives inline children their own session plus PR_SET_PDEATHSIG SIGKILL so a SIGKILLed caller group takes the tree down, persists child pid/pgid/start identity right after spawn, and TERM-then-KILLs only identity-matched lost-run groups. Evidence: tests/tool/test_wrapper_fidelity.py (owner group kill and inline caller-group SIGKILL leave no sh/sleep survivors; stale pgid is spared) passes against core 04fbb48; live run 595ae05ab7d0fd63c3226bf1dfd6b0dd recorded child_pid/child_pgid/identity at spawn. The sase-16h land moves sase-core-revision.txt to 04fbb48 so CI's core exposes tool_run_observe.
